component.name: Revenant
component.summary: Electronic document signing with ARX CoSign

description.p: Cross-platform client for signing PDF documents via the ARX CoSign SOAP API (OASIS DSS standard). Works on macOS, Linux, and Windows without requiring a Windows-only CoSign client.
Features:

ul.li: Embedded PDF signatures with visual appearance
Detached CMS/PKCS#7 signatures
Pre-computed SHA-1 hash signing
Automatic signer identity discovery from server or signed PDFs
Secure credential storage via system keychain

description.p: Security release. Three fixes covering background results being applied to the wrong thing, and one covering where signed files are written.

ul.li: Cancelling the connection dialog now really cancels it. A slow server could answer after you backed out and still be saved as the active one, sending later logins and signing there.
A saved password is no longer pre-filled into a login it was not read for, and a password box you cleared is not silently filled in again.
Signing no longer writes through a shortcut left at the output location, which could overwrite a different file of yours.

description.p: Security release. Corrects what the app reports about a signature; the command-line tool was not affected.

ul.li: A document altered after signing is no longer reported as a valid signature. The verdict came from the signature alone, so a modified file could show a green result with the integrity failure listed separately beneath it.
A signature that failed to verify no longer shows a signer name or a trusted certificate authority alongside the failure.

description.p: Security release. Completes a size-limit fix that 3.0.2 applied to only one of the three clients.

ul.li: An oversized signature is refused before it is decoded in the Rust client too, not only in the JavaScript one. A crafted document could still exhaust memory during verification on this build.

description.p: Security release. Three fixes in signature verification plus a batch-signing fix; upgrading is recommended.

ul.li: The order certificates appear in a signature no longer decides which one is trusted or shown as the signer. A signature made by an untrusted certificate could be reported as valid and trusted by listing a trusted one ahead of it.
Long-term validation status is no longer claimed on the strength of data that sits outside the signature, where anyone can add it.
An oversized signature is refused before it is decoded, so a crafted document can no longer exhaust memory during verification.
Batch signing reserves every output name before signing and never replaces an existing file, so a queued document can no longer be overwritten by an earlier one's result.

description.p: Security release. Fixes one signature-verification flaw introduced in 3.0.0; upgrading is recommended for everyone running that version.

ul.li: A CMS signature that carries no signed attributes no longer vouches for a document it never covered. Content embedded in the signature blob was preferred over the file being checked, so a genuine signature over other bytes could be reported as valid for an unrelated document.

description.p: Security release. Signature verification is hardened throughout and upgrading is recommended for all users.

ul.li: Signatures are now checked cryptographically, not only for structure, and the signer identity is bound to the certificate the signature was actually made with.
A signing service's response is verified before any workflow reports success.
Unsigned incremental revisions appended to a signed document are detected and reported.
Verification no longer contacts hosts named inside the document being verified.
The legacy TLS transport authenticates the appliance against a pinned key, and is never selected as a fallback after a standard HTTPS failure.

description.p: Fixes a macOS sandbox write failure: the GUI now resolves output paths via native Save/Open dialogs (Powerbox) on every sign operation, granting the app sandbox write permission. Previously, auto-derived paths like Downloads/file_signed.pdf triggered Operation not permitted (os error 1).

The separate output path text field and "Browse..." button are removed -- the destination is chosen directly from the native dialog when clicking "Sign PDF" (single file) or selecting a folder (batch mode).
Bug fix for macOS: the Dock icon is no longer replaced by a flat square while the app is running -- the rounded app icon is used throughout.
Rewritten from the ground up in Rust: self-contained native binaries with no bundled Python runtime, a smaller footprint, and faster start.

ul.li: Native desktop GUI with a live signature-placement preview
Three new interface languages: Turkish, Georgian, and Persian (right-to-left)
In-process certificate-chain validation against the profile's pinned trust anchors

description.p: Completed Armenian locale -- 21 untranslated strings fixed.
PKI certificate chain validation and improved verification UX.

ul.li: Validate signer certificate chains against ETSI Trust Service Lists (TSL)
Human-readable trust status in verify results (trusted / not publicly trusted)
Test coverage expanded to 95%+ (740 tests)

description.p: Improved Russian and Armenian translations, added English locale.
Russian and Armenian localization, signature position preview, friendly error messages, BER signature support.

ul.li: Mac App Store, Homebrew, and DMG now support Intel Macs
Universal binary merging via lipo

ul.li: Configure Microsoft Store identity (Revenant Sign)
Release pipeline now includes MAS .pkg in GitHub Releases
TypeScript/Node.js client (revenant-sign on npm) with 662 tests at 97%+ coverage

Remove version from window title

description.p: Initial alpha release with full signing and verification support.

ul.li: PDF digital signing via CoSign SAPI Web Service (SOAP/DSS)
Embedded visible signatures with customizable appearance
Detached CMS/PKCS#7 signature support
PDF signature verification (embedded and detached)
Cross-platform GUI with sign, verify, and setup dialogs
CLI with sign, verify, check, info, and setup commands
Multi-profile configuration with secure credential storage
Armenian font support (GHEA Grapalat, GHEA Mariam)
Legacy TLS 1.0 transport for EKENG appliance
